probe.prompt: How do plants and animals help each other with the air we breathe?

answer: Plants and animals work together to keep the air we breathe clean. Most of the oxygen in the air is made by plants, trees, and tiny plants in the sea through photosynthesis. So caring for trees and oceans helps keep the air we breathe clean! Many water plants have spongy tissue full of air spaces inside their leaves and stalks. This air keeps them light and buoyant, and also carries oxygen down to the roots in the airless mud. Bees, butterflies, and birds help pollination by carrying pollen from one flower to another. probe.prompt: Why does ice float on water if it's a solid? I thought solids were heavier.
probe.intent: English reasoning; counter-intuitive, correct the premise.
must_cover: ice is less dense than water

answer: Ice floats on water because it is lighter than the same amount of liquid water! Ice is made of water, but it is also less dense — solid ice has less water packed into it. So, in the same volume, the ice is lighter than the water it floats on. That's why it floats! Which makes ice the 'super-light' of all materials.
samples: Ice floats on water because it is lighter than the same amount of liquid water! Ice is made of water, but it is also less dense — solid ice has less water packed into it. So, in the same volume, the ice is lighter than the water it floats on. That's why it floats! Which makes ice the 'super-light' of all materials.

probe.prompt: Why does metal feel colder than wood even when they're both in the same room?
probe.intent: English reasoning; same temp, metal conducts heat away. Must NOT say metal is colder.

answer: Metal and wood are at the same temperature, but the metal feels colder. This is because metal is a good conductor, so it quickly pulls heat away from your hand, making it feel cold. Meanwhile, the wood stays warmer. Think of it like a sponge — metal sucks heat away quickly, while wood holds onto some of it.
